    Welfare

    What your student card gets you

    Free Wi-Fi, software, printing and fitness centre, discounts in shops and museums, and medical and accident cover: each line links to its details.

    This page has not been reviewed in over a year

    Some details here may be out of date. Check with the responsible body before relying on them

    On this page

    1. Free
    2. Discounts
    3. Covered by the university
    4. Also available

    Everything here is free or cheaper for Thammasat students. Each line links to the page with the details.

    Free

    What you getIn short
    Wi-Fi across the universitySign in with your student number and national ID number
    Microsoft Office, Canva Pro and Adobe Creative CloudWith your @dome email
    Computer roomRegister before you use it
    Printing100 baht per person per semester at Pridi Banomyong Library
    Plagiarism and AI checksAt Pridi Banomyong Library and the other libraries
    Space in the Student Activity BuildingFree to book, 09:00 to 20:30
    Lan Pridi and your faculty's common roomFree for activities, and free for your own faculty's students
    Fitness centreFree for Thammasat students
    Sanitary products and condomsFree
    Shuttle to Pinklao and MRT Sanam ChaiFree, Monday to Friday

    Discounts

    What you getIn short
    Bookshop, cafés and restaurants10% off at the bookshop and at several cafés and restaurants
    MuseumsFree entry or half price at the museums listed
    TU-GET and TOEICA student rate set by your student ID year, and TOEIC at 1,400 baht

    Covered by the university

    What you getIn short
    Medical and dental costsUp to set limits each visit and each academic year
    Accident insuranceTreatment, disability and death cover, with nothing to pay up front at contracted hospitals
    Emergency grants5,000 baht if you are affected by border conflict or a disaster

    Also available

    • Borrow books, board games and blankets, and book rooms: Library opening hours and services
    • Borrow a laptop, charger or calculator: Borrow a laptop, charger or calculator
    • Talk to a counsellor: Talk to someone about how you feel
